candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — geriatric antihistamine adverse effects
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that older adults are especially susceptible to diphenhydramine-related dizziness, sedation, and hypotension and require medication-safety assessment and teaching.

options.A: Older adults are more susceptible to dizziness, sedation, and hypotension from diphenhydramine, so the prescription warrants caution and safety assessment.
options.B: Older adults usually develop less sedation and dizziness from diphenhydramine than younger adults, so age reduces concern about adverse effects.
options.C: Diphenhydramine improves alertness in older adults despite its antihistamine effects, so it is preferred when allergy treatment must avoid drowsiness.
options.D: Diphenhydramine has no age-related precautions for dizziness or blood-pressure effects, so routine geriatric medication review is unnecessary when it is prescribed.

candidate.rationale: The current prescription diphenhydramine oral-solution label specifically states that antihistamines are most likely to cause dizziness, sedation, and hypotension in elderly patients. A therefore identifies the label-supported geriatric safety concern. B and D deny the labeled age-related risk, and C contradicts the drug's sedative effects.
candidate.source_claim_supported: In elderly patients, antihistamines are most likely to cause dizziness, sedation, and hypotension; diphenhydramine also causes drowsiness/sedation and can reduce alertness.
